sources.citation: Gravina, Richard (2014). The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. LOT 375, sec. 6.3.3 'Bata and Bachama' (p. 146-147)
sources.note: Bachama section (citing Pweddon & Skinner 2001 and Seibert n.d. 'Bachama word list') covers only palatalization/labialization prosodies; the book explicitly excludes tone and stress from its reconstruction ('though not including tone or stress'). Nothing on Bacama stress.

sources.citation: Kraft, Charles H. (1981). Chadic wordlists. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer — Bacama list as digitised in lexibank/kraftchadic v4.1 (CC-BY-4.0), Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13832124
sources.note: Wordlist only: 437 Bacama forms, 371 carry grave/acute tone diacritics (e.g. ŋgà fùda ɗìye 'blow', nɔrò 'plait'); no statement about stress.

sources.citation: Carnochan, Jack (1975). Bachama and Chadic. In J. Bynon & T. Bynon (eds.), Hamito-Semitica (proceedings of the 1970 SOAS colloquium), pp. 459-468. The Hague: Mouton. DOI 10.1515/9783111356167.459
sources.note: Comparative (Proto-Chadic consonant correspondences) paper. Marks Bachama words with tone patterns, e.g. p. 460: 'they call themselves ɓwa:re (low-mid tones).. bacama (mid-high-high).. hama bacama (mid-mid-mid-high-high)'; no mention of stress or accent anywhere in the chapter; p. 468 closes: 'the first task is to produce a detailed phonological study of Bachama itself.'

tone.quote: in fact, they call themselves 5wa:re (low-mid tones), which is the plural of bwa:m (low-mid) masculine and 5 wa:mto (low-low-mid) feminine. The word bacama (mid-high-high) is the name they give to the town shown on maps as Lamurde, the normal home of their chief, whose title is hama bacama (mid-mid-midhigh-high) ‘Chief of Bachama’ … They refer to their speech as kwa: bwa:te (mid-low-mid) ‘mouth of people’. … But the first task is to produce a detailed phonological study of Bachama itself.
tone.says: Tone is transcribed on Bachama words with low, mid and high pitch labels (elsewhere with H/L marks), but no available description states the tone inventory or analyses the system.

sources.locator: p. 95, end of section 2; Ɓacama data in section 4.2, Tables 26-28, pp. 114-116
sources.note: No statement of the Bacama tone system. The p. 95 passage (verified verbatim) is the author's tone-marking policy for all ten languages treated ('In some languages, many of the morphemes concerned.. are inherently toneless') and is not said of Bacama specifically. Section 4.2 'Bacama' (pp. 114-116) gives a short segmental note (two phonemic vowels /a/ and /schwa/, /schwa/ -> [e] before pause) and plural morphology; Table 28 (verbal plurals, data from Gabriel [Wama] 2020) carries acute/grave marks on each vowel (e.g. [kip@] H-L 'lose' sg vs [kep@] pl, [ka] H 'throw' vs [kala] L-H pl), Tables 2…

sources.citation: Carnochan, Jack. 1970. A note on the vowels of Bachama. In Bohuslav Hála, Milan Romportl & Přemysl Janota (eds.), Proceedings of the Sixth International Congress of Phonetic Sciences, held at Prague, 7-13 September 1967, 235-236. Prague: Academia, Publishing House of the Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences.
sources.note: No statement of the tone inventory; the note treats singular/plural verb-stem vowel alternations and concord; every example sentence is followed by a hand-drawn pitch-pattern line (e.g. ex. 1-19), i.e. pitch is transcribed but not analysed here. Congress discussion appended.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth International Congress of Phonetic Sciences, held at Prague
